preview: Football's back, and the Hogs open the Ryan Silverfield era against a North Alabama team the Razorbacks have somehow never played before. Vegas has Arkansas favored by about 40..... Not much history here... actually zero.

Credit where it's due: North Alabama is the only school in America with a live lion living on campus, they won three straight Division II national titles back in the '90s, and this fall they finally moved into a brand-new stadium in Florence after 76 years in an old one. We'll call that a win for them. That said — they went 2-10 last year (sound familiar), they're breaking in new coordinators on both sides, and Silverfield already knows their defensive line coach from his Memphis days.

Fun side plot: Bobby Petrino is calling plays at North Carolina now, had 2 turnovers in his opener, and got flagged 11 times — tape Silverfield reportedly showed the team as a "do NOT do this" reel. Bobby did pick up the win though.
Kickoff 3:15, tailgate starts around 11:00. Menu's Shilo's Tacos.

No. 2 Georgia (2-0) opens SEC play at 11 a.m. on ABC against a 1-1 Arkansas team still finding its feet. The Hogs won the Silverfield debut 31-14 over North Alabama, then got worked 43-10 in Utah. Vegas has the Dawgs by about 25.

Georgia put up 63 and 70 the last two weeks. Gunner Stockton has 8 touchdown passes and zero picks. Silverfield said this week they don't have many flaws, and the tape agrees. Last time they were in Fayetteville was 2020: Georgia 37, Arkansas 10. Last meeting was 2021 in Athens: 37-0. We did beat them in the 1969 Sugar Bowl and the 1976 Cotton Bowl, if you're looking for a historical coping mechanism.
This is a home SEC opener in a packed house. Hang around, run it better than last Saturday, and let 76,000 people remind them they're on the road. KJ Jackson is still the quarterback.
